channel.title: Bloomberg — Reuters/Bloomberg pool
channel.description: Provenance-aware feed; classification fields distinguish exact wire copies from citations.

item.title: Why Long-Dated Bonds Are at Epicenter of Investor Angst
item.description: Yields on 30-year US Treasuries rose to the highest since 2007 this week, while French borrowing costs hit the loftiest since 2008 and their German peers traded at 2011 levels. While domestic factors have a role in each market, the structural forces driving up yields are global in nature, as Bloomberg's Ven Ram explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Alibaba Shares Jump 5% as Alipay Launches New Merchant Platform
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. shares rose the most in two weeks as the launch of a new ecommerce platform boosted optimism toward the company before its June quarter earnings this week.
item.dc:creator: Jeanny Yu

item.title: JPMorgan's Faller Sees US Driving Equity Market Gains
item.description: Madison Faller, investment strategist at JPMorgan Private Bank, says the US "remains core for portfolios" given its exposure to growth and innovation, economic resilience and higher corporate profit margins. When it comes to Europe, "we would be taking more of a selective approach around the sectors that we like," Faller tells Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Removes Microsoft Windows at State Users Ahead of Plan
item.description: China is pulling the plug on an older version of Microsoft Corp.’s Windows tailored for government agencies, taking another step toward rooting out the world’s most popular PC software in a broader effort to reduce its dependence on foreign technology.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Why China's DeepSeek, Qwen and Moonshot Are a Worry for US AI Rivals
item.description: Chinese AI models are cheaper and more adaptable than the preeminent US platforms, and studies suggest they’re now almost as proficient. How did that happen?
item.dc:creator: Saritha Rai

item.title: Korea Jettisons Startup From High-Stakes Sovereign AI Contest
item.description: South Korea eliminated a team led by Motif Technologies Co. from its sovereign AI competition, narrowing the high-stakes contest to three remaining groups.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee

item.title: Korea Denies Report on Discussing Chips as First US Investment
item.description: South Korea denied a local media report that the government is discussing a semiconductor project as the first investment under its $350 billion commitment to the US.
item.dc:creator: Heesu Lee

item.title: Xiaomi Earnings Key to Extending Stock’s Best Rally In a Year
item.description: Xiaomi Corp. shares may extend their best quarterly performance in over a year if its earnings report shows it’s gotten a handle on rising material expenses.
item.dc:creator: Charlotte Yang

item.title: Alphabet’s Australian Bond Offers Pickup Over Dollar Debt
item.description: Alphabet Inc. started marketing its debut Australian debt, offering investors a pickup over what they’d get on its US dollar notes, as the tech giant embarks on another multi-billion dollar fundraising amid skyrocketing AI spending.
item.dc:creator: Finbarr Flynn, Matthew Burgess and Sharon Klyne

item.title: Stocks & Bonds Fall as Oil Rises on Geopolitical Tensions | The Close 8/17/2026
item.description: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Morgan Stanley Private Wealth Management Executive Director Katerina Simonetti, S&P Global Ratings Chief Analytical Officer for Governments Nora Wittstruck, Former PepsiCo President Derek Lewis, BNP Paribas US Head Equity & Derivative Strategy Greg Boutle, JPMorgan Asset Management Global Alternatives Strategist Aaron Mulvihill, Advent International Operating Partner Kahina Van Dyke, & Citi Retailing/Broadlines & Hardlines Analyst Steven Zaccone. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Facebook, Instagram Under Scrutiny in Meta Social Media Addiction Trial
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. is headed to court Tuesday for a high-stakes showdown with a coalition of state attorneys general over claims that the company deliberately designed Facebook and Instagram to encourage compulsive use among young users.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: Big Take: How Amazon Landed On Mamdani's Labor Agenda
item.description: On today’s Big Take podcast, reporters Spencer Soper and Josh Eidelson join Sarah Holder to discuss why New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is challenging the subcontractor model Amazon relies on for last-mile deliveries — and how the move could challenge corporate America’s reliance on subcontractors more broadly. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mexico Explores Ways to Regulate Social Media Among Children
item.description: Mexico is exploring ways to regulate the use of social media by children and adolescents, as countries such as Australia and Brazil have done, with government-led discussions on the harmful effects of platforms like Instagram and TikTok.
item.dc:creator: Alex Vasquez

item.title: Kahina Van Dyke on Stablecoins, Fintech Consolidation
item.description: Romaine Bostick sat down with Kahina Van Dyke, Advent International Operating Partner and Owner of the Inkwell Beach House, from Bloomberg's New Voices Initiative from Martha's Vineyard. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic’s Annualized Revenue Tops $65 Billion Before IPO
item.description: Anthropic PBC is on track to generate annualized revenue of more than $65 billion based on its current performance, according to people familiar with the matter, up more than sevenfold from its pace at the end of last year.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas, Rebecca Torrence and Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: KKR’s Internet Brands Readies Debt Refinancing in Near Term
item.description: KKR & Co.-owned Internet Brands is planning to issue a bond as soon as in the next few weeks to refinance debt and capitalize on its improved business performance, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reshmi Basu and Irene García Pérez

item.title: Bedrock Brings Autonomous Driving to Construction
item.description: Bedrock Robotics is bringing autonomous driving technology to construction sites, retrofitting excavators and other heavy machinery with cameras, LiDAR, Nvidia-powered compute and its own software. CEO Boris Sofman joins Bloomberg to discuss the company’s first paid commercial deployments, how autonomous equipment could address a growing shortage of skilled operators, and why demand for data centers and other infrastructure is creating an opportunity to use AI to help America build faster. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The World’s Richest Families Bet on SpaceX
item.description: Some of the world’s wealthiest families are building significant positions in SpaceX. Bloomberg’s Devon Pendleton breaks down roughly $3.8 billion in holdings disclosed by about a dozen family offices, including investors tied to the Pritzker dynasty, UAE royalty and global hedge fund and mining fortunes. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stripe to Buy AI Firm OpenRouter in $7 Billion Deal
item.description: Stripe is making one of its biggest AI bets yet, agreeing to buy OpenRouter for more than $7 billion, according to sources. Bloomberg’s Natasha Mascarenhas explains how OpenRouter helps developers access and optimize hundreds of AI models, why that capability has become increasingly valuable as companies focus on lowering AI costs, and what the deal signals about Stripe’s ambitions in AI. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Will Back First Phase of OpenAI Ohio Project With as Much as $105 Billion
item.description: Nvidia Corp. has agreed to spend as much as $105 billion to support a massive new data center campus in Ohio set to be leased by OpenAI, marking the latest tie-up between two dominant forces driving the AI boom.
item.dc:creator: Ian King and Will Wade
